text:
mira: hey everyone, first-week question — I accidentally used a hosted API key for local testing and then rotated it; my dev scripts started returning 401s. Should new hires ever use hosted keys on their laptops? Also hitting 429s in CI when running integration tests, any quick mitigations? :confused:

devon: short answer: avoid hosted keys for local dev. Use sandbox keys for day-to-day work. Hosted keys are production-grade, billed, and should live in secrets stores for staging/prod only. For CI 429s: either request a repo-scoped CI sandbox key or throttle tests and add retry/backoff.

mira: where do I create a sandbox key? the Console UI only showed "Hosted API Key" initially.

leah: Console -> API Keys -> Create sandbox key. SSO role propagation can lag a few minutes after onboarding; if you still don't see it, open a ticket in #devex and mention your org role.

mira: ok found it. For local dev, is it ok to set the env var directly?

devon: yes for short-term dev, set an env var like `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<sandbox-key>"` and never commit it. For CI, put the key in the repo's secrets store. Example: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`

mira: about CI 429s — is there a template for requesting extra quota?

leah: use the #devex template: `Quota/key request - repo:<repo>, purpose:<CI|staging|pairing>, expected RPS:<n>, duration:<24h|72h|other>, contact:@<handle>` . We usually grant small per-repo CI sandbox keys for 24–72h for onboarding.

mira: one more thing — I was streaming a long generation and got a 429 mid-stream. Is that expected?

devon: yes, streaming still consumes tokens; if you hit a quota mid-request you'll see a 429. Mitigations: reduce `max_tokens` during dev, split long generations into multiple calls, or run on a staging key for heavy experiments. Also honor `Retry-After` and implement jittered exponential backoff on 429s.

infra-bot: :warning: Security reminder: hosted API keys must not be committed or shared outside approved secrets stores. If a hosted key is leaked, rotate it immediately and notify security@redwood.ai. Automated scanners will flag exposures.

leah: quick onboarding checklist for keys: 1) use sandbox keys locally, 2) never commit hosted keys, 3) store CI keys in secrets (Vault/GH Actions), 4) implement retry/backoff and honor Retry-After, 5) request CI sandbox quota via #devex with template, 6) rotation order for hosted keys: create new key -> update secrets store -> restart consumers -> revoke old key.

mira: perfect, saved the checklist and filing the quota request now. thanks all! :thumbsup:
